meta.requirement: Explore Sal Terrae (10%+ exploration) to trigger this quest.

customTabs.label: TIP
customTabs.content:
You can click the '''Collapse''' button and the '''Best Route''' → '''Important Only''' button at the top to minimize it.
''Some quests will not have a Best Route choice, because the best choice is subjective or not yet found.''

You can also click the '''Endings''' button at the top to view all possible endings, and clicking an ending will show the options needed to reach that ending.

start.title: Saltflame Rite
start.text:
''The salt flats of Sal Terrae hold the afternoon heat like a closed oven. Nothing grows here. The crust is white and cracked to the horizon, and the only shade for a mile is the long shadow of a traveler in Liyue garb, kneeling at the center of a ring of salt crystals laid flat against the ground.''

''She has a catalyst raised in both hands. Her lips move through a count you cannot hear over the wind. Around her, three Pyro Slimes drift along the edge of the ring, pulsing orange with each number she speaks, and the crystals beneath them have begun to glow from within.''

Mei: ''without breaking rhythm, eyes shut'' If you are going to stand in my light, stranger, then either help or step back. These three have decided my salt is supper.

''The nearest slime presses against the ritual line and recoils, hissing a thread of steam.''

choices.label: What are you doing out here?

I_will_clear_them_off.text:
Mei: ''a sharp breath'' Good. Keep them off the ring. I am a few counts from setting this batch, and I will not lose it to blobs with appetites.

''She bows her head back to the glowing crystals. All three Pyro Slimes turn from her at once, shells flaring bright as forge-coals, and roll toward you across the salt.''

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Defeat the Pyro Slimes circling Mei's rite at Sal Terrae

continues.label: Do /rpg again and then click on Fight the Pyro Slimes. Defeat 3 [[Pyro Slime]]s

whacchu_doin_here.text:
Mei: ''still counting under her breath, words slotted between the numbers'' Sealing a formula. Salt binds fire, if you let it set. ''four, five'' My master taught me that. The slimes can smell the heat coming off the work, and they want it.

''She risks one glance up at you. Her eyes are red-rimmed and tired in a way the sun has nothing to do with.''

Mei: I cannot hold the count and the circle both. Decide quickly.

killed_slimes.text:
''The last slime bursts into sparks and a fine drift of salt that the wind carries south. The flats go quiet. Mei's count falters, then stops.''

''Beneath her hands the crystals are not cooling. They have cracked, hairline fractures spidering out from the center, and a thread of red light bleeds up through them before it gutters and dies.''

Mei: ''staring at the ruined ring, voice flat'' That should not have happened. The salt should have held.

''She sits back on her heels and presses the heel of her hand against her eyes.''

Mei: You saved the batch. I am not certain the batch was worth saving.

choices.label: The salt nearly split. What is this, really?

nearly_split.text:
Mei: ''quiet, not looking at you'' It is a Fireball formula. A real one, controlled, the kind you can teach without burning down the room. My master spent thirty years on it. He wanted it entered in the Church registry in Mondstadt, recognized across Teyvat, not just another trick out of some Liyue back-alley.

''She turns the catalyst over and over in her hands.''

Mei: He died in the spring with the last step unwritten. So I have been finishing it. ''a brittle pause'' And I have been changing it. Making it hotter than he ever wanted. That is why the salt cracked. That is why the slimes came. I keep telling myself he would approve, and I keep knowing that he would not.

''She finally looks up, and the question is already plain on her face before she asks it.''

Mei: So tell me, traveler. How do you finish a thing your teacher left unfinished?

choices.label: Finish it the way he meant it. Cool and safe
Keep your version. The power is real, don't waste it
Maybe it isn't yours to finish. Let it rest with him

finish_the_way_he_mean.text:
Mei: ''something loosens across her shoulders'' Cool and safe. The way he wrote it. ''a small, wet laugh'' I have been fighting that answer for a month.

''She sweeps the cracked crystals aside and lays a fresh ring, slower this time, setting each one by hand. When she begins the count again her voice is lower and steadier, and the salt drinks the heat instead of fighting it. No glow. No slimes. Just a clean white ring going quietly inert.''

''She lifts a wax-sealed scroll from the salt and presses it into your hands. The wax is barely warm.''

Mei: Take it to Sister Victoria at the Cathedral. Tell her Master Yan's saltflame rite is finished, and that his apprentice asks for it to be entered under his name. Not mine.

''She wipes her face with the back of her wrist and almost smiles.''

Mei: Go on. He waited thirty years. He can wait the walk to Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Carry Mei's sealed formula to Sister Victoria at the Mondstadt Cathedral

continues.label: Go to Mondstadt City (Mondstadt), do /rpg and click on Deliver the Formula to the Cathedral

go_mond.text:
''Sister Victoria meets you on the Cathedral steps and takes the scroll without a word at first, turning it to read the seal pressed into the wax.''

Victoria: Saltflame notation. ''she breaks it, scans the first lines, and her eyebrows rise'' Master Yan's hand. I corresponded with him once, years ago, about whether a combat art could be taught without leaving scars on the one who learns it. He believed it could. ''she reads on'' It seems he was right, in the end.

''She lowers the scroll.''

Victoria: His apprentice sent this for the registry, you said. Under his name.

Saltflame_Rite__Formula_Registered.title: Formula Registered
Saltflame_Rite__Formula_Registered.text:
Victoria: ''a slow nod'' Then it will be entered as his. Thirty years of work, recognized in Mondstadt at last. She chose well, sending it here.

''She copies the formula into the registry ledger in a careful hand, then counts silver from the Church fund into your palm.''

Victoria: For carrying it, and for keeping his apprentice from setting the salt flats alight in her grief. When you are ready, ask the Skill Book for Fireball. You will want a Catalyst focus to cast it, but the art itself is yours now.

''She pauses on the threshold, the open doors warm with candlelight behind her.''

Victoria: If you see Mei again, tell her this. Her teacher would have been proud of the restraint. It is the hardest thing to write into a formula, and the hardest thing to choose.

keep_ur_version.text:
Mei: ''something hungry flickers across her face, half guilt, half thrill'' You feel it too. Thirty years of caution, and the one time I let it run hot, the thing actually breathes.

''She does not lay a new ring. She forces the cracked one back to life, hands flat against the broken salt, and pours the count out fast and reckless. The crystals do not glow this time. They blaze. Red light climbs her arms and the air over the flats bends like glass in a kiln.''

Mei: ''teeth gritted, shouting over a rising roar'' It will not set clean. Something is coming up through the heat. Whatever it is, do not let it reach the ring before I bind this.

''The salt crust splits open to the south, and a shape of living fire drags itself up into the light.''

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Contain the saltflame flare before it cracks the Sal Terrae flats

continues.label: Do /rpg again and click on Contain the Saltflame Flare. Defeat 4 [[Pyro Slime]]s

contain_saltbound.text:
''The fire-thing comes apart in a gout of sparks and falls back into the crack it crawled from. The roar drops to a hiss, then to wind. The salt around the ring has fused to black glass, still ticking as it cools.''

''Mei kneels in the middle of it, breathing hard, a wax-dark scroll clutched against her chest. It is sealed. It worked.''

Mei: ''an unsteady laugh'' It held. Barely. ''she looks at the scorched ring, then at you'' The Cathedral will never certify this. It bites the caster, just a little, every time. Victoria would lock it in a drawer and call it mercy.

''She holds the scroll out anyway, and her grin is sharp and tired and real.''

Mei: So we keep it off the books. You earned it out here, not in some ledger. Take it.

Saltflame_Rite__Saltflame_Unbound.title: Saltflame Unbound
Saltflame_Rite__Saltflame_Unbound.text:
''She walks you through the core of it right there on the cooling glass, fast and low, the way you teach a thing you are not supposed to know. The shape of the count. Where the heat lives. How to throw it without throwing yourself in after.''

Mei: ''closing your hand around the scroll'' It will sting your palm the first hundred times. After that you stop noticing, which is its own kind of warning.

''She gathers her things and squints north, toward Liyue and home.''

Mei: I am keeping a copy. I am going to make it worse. ''a real smile'' My master would be furious. I think that is the only reason I am smiling.

''Behind you the ring of black glass cools to the color of old coals. Nothing will grow in that circle for a long season, and the wind that crosses it carries a faint smell of forge-smoke all the way to the road.''

maybe_it_isnt_urs.text:
Mei: ''the catalyst lowers'' Not mine to finish.

''For a moment you think she will throw it at you. Her jaw sets, her eyes go bright and furious, and then all of it goes out of her at once, like a coal dropped into water.''

Mei: ''very quietly'' I came all this way so that I would not have to stop. So I could keep his hands moving through mine. If I seal it, he is finished. If I burn it, he is finished. There was never a count that ended any other way.

''She gathers the cracked crystals into her palm, and the half-written notes with them, and she looks at the dead white crust of Sal Terrae as if seeing it for the first time.''

Mei: Not here. This place is already a grave. Help me take it somewhere the wind still moves. There is a great tree north of the city. Windrise. He would have liked the sound of it.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Travel with Mei to Windrise to scatter her master's unfinished rite

continues.label: Go to Windrise (Mondstadt), do /rpg and click on Scatter the Rite at Windrise

go_windrise.text:
''Windrise stands alone above the plain, its great branches turning the wind into something you can hear. After the dead silence of the salt flats the sound is almost too much, leaves and grass and the far blue line of Cider Lake, all of it moving at once.''

''Mei is already there when you arrive, sitting in the roots with the notes in her lap. She has kept one page, a single sheet covered in a cramped, slanting hand that is not her own.''

Mei: ''not looking up'' His writing. He wrote like he was trying to set the paper on fire. ''she folds the page once, carefully, and tucks it away'' The rest can go.

''She opens her hands over the wind. The salt grains and the loose notes lift and scatter, pale paper turning over and over until the tree takes them out of sight.''

choices.label: Stay with her in the roots a while

Saltflame_Rite__The_Rite_Released.title: The Rite Released
Saltflame_Rite__The_Rite_Released.text:
''You sit. The wind works through the branches and neither of you fills the quiet. Somewhere below, the grass leans all one way and springs slowly back.''

Mei: ''eventually'' I thought letting go would feel like losing. It feels like setting down something I have carried so long I forgot it was heavy.

''She presses a small pouch of coin into your hand, and on top of it a worn catalyst focus, plain and smooth from years of use.''

Mei: His spare. I have no need of two, and you did not laugh at me out there when you had every reason to. ''a tired, honest smile'' The formula stays unwritten. I am at peace with that, which I did not expect to be able to say.

''She stands, brushes the grass from her knees, and turns north toward Liyue and home, lighter by the weight of one unfinished thing.''

''The great tree keeps moving behind you, patient as it has always been, and the wind carries the last of the salt out over the plain.''
